jobs.title: AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST
jobs.description:
Job Posting: Air Pollution Specialist



State Air Resources Board


JC\-529209* 

Air Pollution Specialist
  

AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST
$5,918\.00 \- $11,455\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **9/9/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**


If you have permanent status and have passed probation, you have mandatory reinstatement rights into your former position/classification at the end of this LT appointment.You will be separated from state service if you have not had prior permanent or probationary civil service status. During this 12\-month limited\-term assignment, you may be entitled to receive health, dental, and vision benefits. You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.

  

  

The Monitoring and Laboratory Division (MLD) seeks one enthusiastic Air Pollution Specialist (APS) for its Oil and Gas Emission Monitoring Section (OGEMS) to implement a program required by Senator Bill 567 (SB 567\). SB 567 authorizes the conversion of oil and gas wells to the gravity\-based energy storage wells and requires continuous monitoring for leaks, including, but not limited to methane. This position is an exciting opportunity to contribute to this new program requiring continuous monitoring of leaks from the gravity\-based energy storage wells—helping reduce emissions and health impacts on surrounding communities. Duties include 1\) reviewing and exploring the monitoring technologies which could be applied to leak monitoring for the gravity\-based energy storage wells; 2\) working with the team in OGEMS and California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM) to develop the criteria for leak detection and data reporting; 3\) conducting stakeholder engagement and explaining complex technical requirements in clear, accessible language during workshops, seminars, and meetings with community groups, operators, agencies, and the public; 4\) working with the team to evaluate the pilot program and make recommendations to the Legislature for a framework to implement an ongoing gravity\-based energy storage well program to regulate the operation of gravity\-based energy storage wells.  

  

This position will require the candidate to possess a driver license and to pass defense driving training courses, enroll in the DMV Pull Notice Program, and maintain a “good” driver status. Additionally, the candidate must be willing to travel up to 25 percent of the time, to work in an industrial environment including exposure to air emissions, fumes, heat, and vehicle traffic, and to wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to a hard hat, safety shoes with toe protection, reflective vest, Nomex overalls, hearing protections, gloves, and safety glasses.
  

  

This position will require the employee to pass a pre\-employment physical.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position may be eligible for hybrid in\-office work and in\-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Boards' (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in\-person attendance is also required.


The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in\-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.


**PLP Language:**

**Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025\). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.**


* Requires being stationary, consistent with office work, for extended periods.
* Standard office environment (artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.)
* Daily use of a personal computer, office equipment, and/or telephone.
* Must be able to move/transport items weighing up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* This position will require the candidate to possess a driver license and to pass training courses (including periodic refresher courses) in defensive driving, enroll in the DMV Pull Notice Program and maintain a “good” driver status.
* This position will require the employee to pass a pre\-employment physical.
* This position may require working in an industrial environment including exposure to air emissions, fumes, heat, and vehicle traffic, and to wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to a hard hat, safety shoes with toe protection, reflective vest, Nomex overalls, hearing protections, gloves, and safety glasses.
* Travel may be required.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Contaminated Land (FIFO) - Northern Territory
jobs.description:
* Major Metals Refinery Closure
* 12\-month full time, site\-based project (extension possible)
* FIFO (2:1\) from any Australian location to Nhulunbuy, Northern Territory

 **About the Project**

  

Tetra Tech Coffey is delivering environmental and contaminated land services to support a major metals refinery closure in Northern Territory, a major component of a broader decommissioning program.  

  

Works involve remediation tracking, contaminated materials management, validation of remediation scopes, and compliance oversight in a complex remote industrial environment

 **The Role**

  

We are seeking an experienced (2 to 5 years) Contaminated Land Consultant (field‑based) to provide on\-site soil validation advice and support, sampling supervision, and contaminated materials support during remediation earthworks.  

  

You will work daily alongside the client, providing practical, technically defensible environmental advice to support the remediation objectives and maintain compliance with the Remediation Action Plan.

 **Key Responsibilities**

**Field Delivery**

* Collect soil and surface water samples, to complete contaminated soil and surface water assessments, delineation, and validation sampling.
* Manage and maintain health and safety on a large remediation project with significant heavy plant movements.
* Provide field\-based material advice to the remediation contractor.
* Oversee material tracking and compliance with the remediation action plan and the remediation validation plan.
* Manage unexpected finds and provide advice to the remediation contractor.
* Maintain strong QA/QC and field records.
* Undertake field pH testing
* Work collaboratively with site teams, technical and project management teams based offsite.

 **Contractor Interface**

* Act as the primary site contact for client requests and advice and manage technical delivery of requests in collaboration with the subject matter expert.
* Support daily pre‑starts and toolbox talks.
* Attend regular client meetings.
* Balance production needs with environmental compliance.

 **Reporting \& Compliance**

* Prepare field summaries and contribute to validation reporting.
* Prepare material classification and other technical memorandums, based on ongoing site requirements.
* Maintain chain‑of‑custody and coordinate laboratories.
* Support EMP, HSE, and regulatory compliance obligations.

  

  

**About You**  

  

**You'll have:**

* You'll be a qualified Environmental Scientist with 2\-5 years experience in contaminated land consulting.
* Demonstrated experience conducting soil and surface water samples, assessments, delineation, and validation sampling on brownfield/industrial sites.
* Experience supporting civil earthworks.
* Strong documentation and communication skills.
* Current, unrestricted Australian Drivers License.
* Ability to meet company \& project medical requirements.
* Confident working independently in remote FIFO settings.

 **Highly Regarded:**

* NT regulatory knowledge.
* Large‑scale remediation or decommissioning experience.
* FIFO or remote project experience.

 **What We Offer**

* Highly competitive salary; provision of mobilisation costs including flights, camp accommodation and meals.
* 2:1 roster (or 2:2 / 3:1 depending on candidate).
* Opportunity to contribute to one of the Southern Hemisphere’s most significant industrial closure and remediation projects.
* Long\-duration project exposure within a technically complex heavy industrial environment.
* Support from an experienced, highly credentialled Environmental Scientists.

  


**About us**  

  

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high\-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

  

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.  

  

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global 1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000\+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.
